content: The Fellowship of the College of Emergency Medicine (FCEM) is the final examination undertaken by specialists in Emergency Medicine in the United Kingdom and Ireland. This specialty was previously referred to as Accident and Emergency Medicine. Historically, the examination was known as the Fellowship of the Faculty of Accident and Emergency Medicine (FFAEM). To be eligible to sit for the FCEM examination, candidates are generally required to have completed four years of a five-year specialist registrar training program in Emergency Medicine. The examination itself is composed of four distinct components. The clinical component constitutes 50% of the total marks and is further divided into two parts: a Short Answer Question (SAQ) paper and an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE). The management component accounts for 25% of the marks, while the academic component makes up the remaining 25%. The academic portion is equally split between a Clinical Topic Review (CTR) and a Critical Appraisal of a paper from the current medical literature. The latter typically involves evaluating a Randomised Controlled Trial, a Systematic Review, or a diagnostic study. It is mandatory for candidates to pass the clinical component of the examination. The FCEM examination is conducted twice annually, with the SAQ paper administered one month prior to the other components of the exam. Successful candidates are awarded the title of Fellows of the College of Emergency Medicine and are entitled to use the post-nominal letters FCEM.
